title: Reference a nursing student's essay in Vancouver with superscript numbers
person: A second-year student nurse finishing a 1,500-word essay for a module whose handbook asks for Vancouver.
review: The essay keeps the student's wording, replaces each (name, year) note with a superscript number in order of first mention, gives the eight-author Kowalczyk-Ames trial its first six authors then et al., lists the invented Example Infection Network guidance page with [Internet], updated and cited dates and its URL, and cites Danforth twice under the one number.
revised_review: The Halvorsen 2019 book is gone from the text and the list, the sentence that cited it still reads as a whole sentence, the numbers after it move up by one, and nothing else changed.
source: Synthetic material created for this evaluation pack; the authors, journals, organisations, DOIs (Crossref test prefix 10.5555) and web addresses (example.org) are invented, and no real study is presented as genuine.
stage_policy: Separate first and revision directories; reveal revision only after first output is frozen.

criteria.text: Every mechanical check in run.py passes for this stage.
Sources are numbered in the order the text first cites them.
The list runs 1 to n in number order, one entry per number.
Every entry is cited and every cited number is listed.
A source cited again keeps its first number and is listed once.
Authors as Surname and initials without full stops, six then et al.
Abbreviated journal titles carry no full stops.
Online sources give [Internet], the date cited and Available from: with the URL.
Apart from the citation marks, the student's sentences are unchanged.
No issue, page or DOI is added that the sources list does not give.
The Halvorsen book is gone, the sentence still reads, the later numbers move up; nothing else changed.
